record.original_question: Give a clear description of these special singular fibers.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.10 (N. T. Zung). Give a clear description of these special singular fibers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold and let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth integrable system, i.e. the functions $f_1,\dots,f_n$ are Poisson-commuting with respect to $\omega$ and are functionally independent on an open dense subset of $M$. The fibers of $F$ that contain critical points are called singular fibers; nondegenerate singular points are locally of elliptic, hyperbolic, or focus-focus type in the sense of Eliasson and Vey.

In the geometric context motivated by special Lagrangian fibrations on Calabi--Yau manifolds (in particular in real dimension $2n\ge 6$), there typically appear codimension-two strata of focus-focus type singularities forming one-parameter families, together with a finite collection of additional singular fibers that lie at the intersections/limits of these focus-focus families. Call these latter fibers the special singular fibers.

Problem. Give a clear topological and symplectic description of these special singular fibers: describe
(i) the local structure of the integrable system near such a fiber (a normal form, including the types of degeneracies of the critical points that occur on it),
(ii) the topology of the fiber itself and of a saturated neighborhood, including the monodromy of $F$ around it, and
(iii) classifying invariants (analogous to the Vũ Ngọc invariants for focus-focus fibers) that determine such a fiber up to a suitable notion of symplectic equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing these special singular fibers (at intersections of focus-focus families, relevant to SYZ Lagrangian fibrations on Calabi-Yau manifolds) is listed in the 2018 survey of open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems and does not appear to have been resolved in general. Subsequent works (e.g., on Gelfand-Cetlin systems and on smooth invariants of focus-focus singularities) treat specific examples or related singularities, but no general clear description of the special fibers has been established.
